Phase I / Phase II SPC applied to batch summaries.
The theory is in Montgomery (*Introduction to Statistical Quality Control*, Ch. 5).
This page covers the implementation in **machinelogR**.

---

## spc_baseline() -- Phase I

```r
bl_pump <- spc_baseline(phase1_data, variable = "pump_load", time_col = "batch_date")
```

Computes the center line and control limits from a reference population.
Returns a frozen baseline object: `CL`, `UCL`, `LCL`, `sigma`.
Computed once. Passed explicitly to Phase II.

Three decisions go into Phase I:

**Which batches.** Batches that represent normal operation.
Exclude known anomalies, equipment changes, formulation adjustments.

**Which variable.** A summary statistic per batch -- mean, maximum, standard deviation.
Mean pump load for gradual mechanical wear. Maximum product temperature for collapse risk.
The choice is made before running the chart, not after.

**When to re-baseline.** On a validated change (equipment replacement, process improvement).
Not on data drift -- re-baselining on drift hides the signal.

---

## spc_chart() -- Phase II

```r
chart <- spc_chart(
  data     = metrics,
  variable = "pump_load",
  time_col = "batch_date",
  rules    = 5L,       # Nelson R5
  cl_from  = bl_pump   # Phase I baseline (frozen)
)
```

`cl_from` takes the object returned by `spc_baseline()`.
Passing the same data to both `data` and `cl_from` defeats the purpose -- the separation is structural.

`rules` accepts a scalar or vector of integers (1 to 8). All eight Nelson rules are implemented.

Return value:

```r
chart$violations      # tibble: date, index, rule fired
chart$control_limits  # list: CL, UCL, LCL, sigma
chart$n_violations    # integer
chart$plot            # patchwork: I-chart + MR chart
```

---

## Which rules to apply

The `rules` argument translates directly to the degradation mode you are monitoring for.

| Degradation mode | `rules` | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Abrupt failure | `1L` | Single point breach is sufficient |
| Gradual wear | `c(5L, 6L)` | Slow drift, never reaches 3-sigma |
| Mean shift | `c(1L, 2L)` | Jump then persistence |
| Sensor drift | `c(3L, 5L)` | Monotone or asymmetric drift |
| Sensor stuck | `7L` | Variance collapses |
| Mixed / unknown | `c(1L, 5L)` | Pragmatic minimum |

---

## In practice

The pump load scenario from [FDSim](fdsim.html): drift injected at batch 17, deviation at batch 50.
A slow, asymmetric increase that never reaches 3-sigma until the equipment is well into its failure trajectory.
That is what R5 is for.

```r
rules = c(1L, 5L)
```
